annotations.title: Check which domain names are free

description: Checks whether domain names are free to register. Pass full domains (bakkerijjansen.nl) and/or bare names (bakkerijjansen); a bare name is tried with every extension in `extensions`, or by default with the ones people ask for most: nl, com, eu, be, de, net, org, shop, online, site, store, tech, app, dev, io, ai, co.uk, uk, fr, at, ch, it, es, nu, se, co, me, info, biz, xyz, cloud. We sell 718 extensions in all (.amsterdam, .restaurant, .photography and so on); pass them in `extensions` when they fit the name. At most 50 domains per call. The first check is quick and asks DNS only: taken means the domain has nameservers (certain); likely_available means it has none, so it is probably free (reason dns_only, or no_rdap where the registry has no RDAP and verifying adds nothing). Once the person has favourites, call again with verify: true for the dns_only ones (at most 10 domains): that asks our registrar (or else the registry over RDAP) and turns them into available or taken; otherwise reason says why (rdap_rate_limited, rdap_unavailable). A premium name (premium: true) costs what its registry asks: price is our price for it in euro cents before VAT, often far above the usual price, so tell the person. unknown means no answer at all. Each free domain has a register_url: a page where the person signs in and registers it in their own name. Registration itself checks again. Each taken domain has a transfer_url: if the domain is the person's own, they move it to Spaicely there.

extensions.description: Extensions to try bare names with, such as nl, com, eu. Default: the ones people ask for most.

names.description: Domains or bare names, such as bakkerijjansen.nl or bakkerijjansen

verify.description: Deep check for a shortlist: also ask the registries. At most 10 domains.
